name: Tomcat Nov release
tile_line: CISA says 9.1, Apache says Low. Off-by-default features.
tldr: Apache disclosed 11 Tomcat bugs on 19 Nov 2026. None has a public exploit or attacks, and all but one need a feature you turn on; the "9.1 critical" is CISA's score, Apache rates it Low. Update Tomcat; TLS-PSK clusters stay on TLS 1.2.
summary: Apache rates the 11 as 1 critical, 4 important, 2 moderate and 4 low. The features you'd have to turn on include HTTP/2, the RewriteValve and clustering. Two cluster bugs aren't fixed: one fix is due in the next releases, and Apache has deprecated the EncryptInterceptor behind the other instead of fixing it.

affected.label: Tomcat before 11.0.29 / 10.1.62 / 9.0.124
affected.text: Every earlier 11.0, 10.1 and 9.0 release; end-of-life 8.5 and older get no fixes. The critical cluster bug is the exception: it affects only 11.0.29, 10.1.62 and 9.0.124. Spring Boot embeds Tomcat, and its newest releases (4.2.0, 4.1.3 and 4.0.10) still bring in 11.0.27; check with `./mvnw dependency:tree -Dincludes=org.apache.tomcat.embed`.

affected.label: You turned on an affected feature
affected.text: Ten of the 11 need something you add: HTTP/2 (an `Http2Protocol` line inside a `<Connector>`; in Spring Boot, `server.http2.enabled`), the RewriteValve, the ExpiresFilter, CGI, Jakarta Authentication, clustering, an AJP load balancer or the OWB module. The shipped files contain commented-out examples, so matches inside `<!-- -->` don't count. Check your apps' `WEB-INF/web.xml` and `META-INF/context.xml` too. The eleventh, a low-rated memory leak (CVE-2026-118233), needs an app that uses the HTTP upgrade API; Apache only says "some circumstances".

do.label: Upgrade to 11.0.29, 10.1.62 or 9.0.124
do.text: Released 13 to 16 Nov 2026, these fix 9 of the 11 bugs; the two cluster bugs aren't fixed in them (see below). Tomcat 8.5 gets no fixes (end of life since 31 Mar 2024), and 9.0 support ends on 31 Mar 2027.

do.label: Spring Boot: set the Tomcat version
do.text: No Spring Boot release brings in a fixed Tomcat yet. Set the `tomcat.version` property to `11.0.29` in your build, the documented way to override a version Spring Boot manages. HTTP/2 is off unless you set `server.http2.enabled`.

do.label: Clusters: stay on TLS 1.2
do.text: If your cluster uses TLS-PSK, keep it on TLS 1.2: on TLS 1.3 a node without the key can join (CVE-2026-133325). The fix comes in 11.0.30, 10.1.63 and 9.0.125; Apache hasn't announced a date, and we'll check again by 28 Nov 2026. The old EncryptInterceptor isn't fixed (CVE-2026-95517) and Apache has deprecated it: move to TLS-PSK on TLS 1.2.

do.label: Don't panic over the 9.1
do.text: The scary numbers come from CISA's automated scoring added to the CVE records, not from Apache: 9.1 on CVE-2026-116561, which Apache rates Low, meaning "extremely hard to exploit" or with "minimal consequences". Apache's own ratings: one critical (the cluster bug), four important.

bugs.title: Cluster TLS-PSK on TLS 1.3 lets any node join
bugs.text: Only clusters secured with TLS-PSK on TLS 1.3, and only on 11.0.29, 10.1.62 and 9.0.124 (Apache also lists 11.0.28, which was never released). No fixed release yet: use TLS 1.2 until 11.0.30, 10.1.63 or 9.0.125.

bugs.title: HTTP/2 connection setup can cause a DoS
bugs.text: Only with HTTP/2 turned on: it's commented out in the shipped `server.xml` and off by default in Spring Boot. Apache: a resource isn't released during HTTP/2 connection setup, which "could lead to a DoS".

bugs.title: Rewrite rules don't stop the request
bugs.text: Only with the RewriteValve (off by default) and a rule using the [F], [G] or [R] flag. Tomcat keeps processing a request such a rule should have stopped; Apache calls it execution after redirect.

bugs.title: ExpiresFilter strips Cache-Control: private
bugs.text: Only with the ExpiresFilter (not in the default `web.xml`) on pages behind Tomcat's login. It removes the header Tomcat sets so proxies don't cache protected pages; it matters if a shared cache or CDN sits in front.

bugs.title: WebSocket memory leak with the OWB module
bugs.text: Only with Tomcat's optional OpenWebBeans (OWB) module and WebSocket. The module isn't shipped as a download; you have to build it from source.
